text:
Sam: Quick check-in — I'm drafting a small follow-up to the observability gating RFC. Proposal: gate high-cardinality trace attributes at the obs gateway by default (drop unless allow-listed per service/route). Main goals: stop unbounded cardinality explosions, make cost predictions reliable, and give teams a clear interface for opt-in. Thoughts?

Lina: I like the direction. Two immediate questions: 1) billing/tenant attributes need to always pass through (can't break chargeback). 2) What about owners who rely on ad-hoc attrs for debugging? we need a preview mode.

Omar: Agree on billing keys — treat them as a global safe-list. Also: we should avoid throwing away values that look like PII; better to hash/redact and emit a marker so teams can request a replay.

Payton: Rollout concerns: suggest feature-flagged rollout + per-service toggles. Canary in staging for 48h, then 10% of prod traffic for a week. We should emit metrics: `ingest.attr_gating.dropped_total`, `ingest.attr_gating.preview_sampled`, and a per-service breakdown.

Sam: Early config sketch (for discussion):
```
attribute_gating:
  default_policy: drop          # drop unless allowed
  global_allow_list: [billing_key, tenant_id, env]
  service_overrides:
    payments: allow           # full pass-through for payments
    auth: redact_except(billing_key)
  preview_sampling_pct: 0.1  # percent of traces that include full attrs for preview
```

Lina: +1 to `preview_sampling_pct`. Also propose a `soft_gate` mode: instead of dropping, redact + keep hash + emit `attr_redacted=true`. That preserves debugability and still reduces cardinality for query indexes.

Omar: Performance note: doing gating at the gateway adds CPU/serialize work but saves downstream storage/ingest costs. We should benchmark with realistic trace sizes. Also keep a low-retention debug store (7d) where we stash a sampled copy of dropped attr values for 1% of keys so SRE can reconstruct issues.

Payton: Ops checklist to include in the RFC: rollout plan, rollback switch, dashboards (dropped_count by service, most-dropped-attr list), alerting when an owner has >1000 new attr values/day, and guidance for teams on migrating attr use to canonical keys.

Sam: Implementation API concerns: 1) How do teams request service-level allow lists? self-serve via console + infra review. 2) How to express patterns? allow-list should support exact keys + regex and reserved namespaces (e.g., `billing_*`). 3) Backwards compatibility: default_policy should be opt-out for 4 weeks after deploy to give teams time to opt-in.

Lina: Good call. Also add a linting job in CI that flags new PRs in services that introduce attr writes outside the canonical set (fail WIP PRs with guidance). That reduces surprise.

Omar: For PII handling: add a safe-regex list and fallback to `sha256(value)` for any flagged attr; log a `pii_hash_skipped` metric when hashing occurs.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: build #4521 started for branch=obs-attr-gating. Tests: gateway-unit, ingest-smoke, telemetry-metrics. (link: https://ci.internal/build/4521)

Sam: I'll add these sections to the RFC: config shape, preview mode, metrics & dashboards, PII handling, rollout checklist, and CI lint. Pinged @Lina @Omar @Payton for review, please add short comments inline. :thumbsup:

Lina: ack

Omar: ack

Payton: ack — will add the canary dashboard prototype later today.
